messages:
tyler: Heads-up — saw a spike in small-allocation rate on canary after the runtime PR (shrink-threshold change). Memory climbs ~200MB over 30m on steady traffic :eyes:

sasha: Link to the flame/pprof? small-alloc spike could be a regressor in the small-object path or arena churn.

tyler: Flamegraph: https://perf.example/graphs/17625-smallalloc.svg
Quick pprof dump I took: `go tool pprof -http=:8080 /tmp/service /tmp/pprof/heap.pb.gz`
Repro command for local: `./bench --concurrency=50 --rps=500 --duration=10m --profile=mem`

maria: Can you capture per-sizeclass hist? For jemalloc we usually do a malloc_stats_print snapshot or run a small wrapper to call `malloc_stats_print` at intervals. If we can't, jeprof-like tools or jemalloc's arena_stats via mallctl can help.

alex: Also try toggling MALLOC_CONF narenas temporarily to see if arenas are the culprit. e.g. `MALLOC_CONF=narenas:8 ./service` — if fragmentation drops it's arena scatter.

tyler: Good call. I can run a canary with MALLOC_CONF=narenas:8 and also with `background_thread:true` off. Want to avoid a full redeploy unless folks agree.

bench-bot: nightly-canary-run 17625 finished — attached mem profile: /artifacts/17625/mem-heap-1.pb.gz (64MB).

sasha: Can someone grab an object-size histogram? We need to know whether it's lots of tiny (~16-64B) allocations increasing, or mid-sized objects. If tiny, string concat/metadata is suspect.

maria: Example mallctl approach (C API call):
```
size_t sz = sizeof(unsigned);
unsigned narenas;
mallctl("arenas.npools", &narenas, &sz, NULL, 0);
// iterate arenas and call malloc_stats_print or arena_stats
```
If you don't want C, I can push a small admin endpoint to call malloc_stats_print and stream it.

tyler: I pushed a branch `smallalloc-debug` that adds `/admin/malloc_stats` guarded by our internal auth. Will run canary with MALLOC_CONF=narenas:8 + that endpoint.

alex: Also try setting `lg_chunk` lower for testing (lg_chunk:20) to reduce internal wastage, but only for repro — may affect perf.

infra-bot: Canary deploy started: service/smallalloc-debug -> canary-42. Trace id: c42-0ab3.

tyler: Capture plan: 1) run canary with MALLOC_CONF=narenas:8 2) hit with bench for 30m 3) pull /admin/malloc_stats and heap pb.gz every 5m 4) compare size histograms and RSS. I'll post results here.

sasha: If you see the small-allocation rate still up with fewer arenas, look at caches (string/Span pools) — a recently merged change toggled a path that avoids reuse.

maria: I'll prepare a tiny tool to convert malloc_stats_print to JSON and annotate with size buckets — should make diffs easier.

tyler: :thumbsup: running step 1 now. I'll update with the first snapshot in ~10m.

bench-bot: bench job started (id b-17625-1).

alex: If this repros we can also run a build with tcmalloc on a local node to see behavior difference. Not for prod, just for signal.

tyler: First snapshot (5m): /artifacts/17625/malloc_stats_5m.json — small-alloc count increased 2.9x vs baseline, biggest buckets 24B and 48B. Posting diff soon.

sasha: Ok that's a clear signal. Likely new allocations from tokenization buffer or header metadata. Tyler, can you grep recent PRs for `appendString` / buffer growth around that timeframe?

tyler: On it. Found one change in PR #5142 where we switched from reusing a scratch buffer to allocating slices per request (was intended to avoid races). Rolling back to reuse seems low risk.

maria: Nice find — try rolling that back in the canary branch and re-run. If RSS drops and small-alloc rate normalizes we can make that fix and add tests.

tyler: Will push patch to `smallalloc-debug` with buffer reuse + additional tests. Re-running bench after patch.

infra-bot: Canary deploy (smallalloc-debug v2) succeeded.

tyler: v2 snapshot (5m): small-alloc count back to baseline, RSS stable. Looks like buffer allocation change was the regressor.

sasha: Great — please open a PR reverting that specific change with a note about the allocator signal. Add perf test in CI to catch regressions (small-alloc histogram assertion).

maria: I'll finish the malloc_stats->JSON tool and add it to perf artifacts.

tyler: Thanks all. Filing the PR now and will follow up with a short postmortem note in eng-runtime.

alex: Nice triage. :rocket:
